long_biography.plain_text:
Arison grew up within an established shipping family and managed its maritime business before moving to the United States. He co-founded Norwegian Caribbean Lines, then struck out independently and launched Carnival Cruise Line in 1972 with a converted ocean liner. Carnival's low-cost, informal approach helped broaden cruising beyond its traditional affluent clientele. Arison bought out an early partner, expanded the fleet and retained a controlling interest when part of the company was offered to public investors.

After handing operational leadership to the next generation, Arison remained connected to Carnival while building Arison Investments in Israel. That holding company acquired interests in banking and construction, adding substantial diversification before his death in 1999. Carnival nevertheless remained the enterprise that created most of his fortune and the clearest principal asset at death. Securities filings show that founder shares later moved through his estate and several family trusts, so successor holdings cannot be treated as assets he continued to own. The Ted Arison Family Foundation is a separate charitable organisation; its endowment and grants were no longer retained personal wealth.
